## Optional Environment Variables (env_accept)

Providers are wired by NAME: a provide is injected only into a consumer that declares the
same name in `env_accept`, so these entries must carry the provider's name verbatim.

| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `OLLAMA_HOST` | Local Ollama server URL (auto-injected by ollama candy `env_provide`) |
| `OPENAI_API_BASE_URL` | OpenAI-compatible API base URL |
| `WEBUI_AUTH` | Enable authentication (default: true) |
| `CHARLY_MCP_SERVERS` | JSON array of MCP servers (auto-injected by `mcp_provide` candies) |
| `CODE_EXECUTION_JUPYTER_AUTH_TOKEN` | Jupyter auth token for the code-execution engine (auto-injected by a jupyter candy `env_provide`) |
| `COMFYUI_BASE_URL` | ComfyUI server base URL, e.g. `http://charly-comfyui-lab:8188` — see *Image generation* below |
| `ENABLE_IMAGE_GENERATION` | Turn image generation on (`true`) once `COMFYUI_BASE_URL` is set |
| `COMFYUI_WORKFLOW_NODES` | JSON map of the workflow nodes carrying prompt/negative_prompt/width/height/batch size/steps/seed. Optional — Open Web UI's own default workflow is used when unset |
| `QWEN3_TTS_HOST` / `QWEN3_TTS_SERVED_MODEL` / `QWEN3_TTS_VOICE` | Speech synthesis provider (auto-injected by a qwen3-tts candy `env_provide`) |
| `WHISPER_BASE_URL` / `WHISPER_MODEL` | Whisper ASR provider (auto-injected by the whisper candy `env_provide`) |
| `QDRANT_URL` | Qdrant REST endpoint (auto-injected by the qdrant layer `env_provide`); with a resolved `QDRANT_API_KEY` it moves the RAG vector store to Qdrant — see *Vector store* below |
| `QDRANT_ON_DISK` / `QDRANT_COLLECTION_PREFIX` / `QDRANT_PREFER_GRPC` / `QDRANT_GRPC_PORT` / `ENABLE_QDRANT_MULTITENANCY_MODE` / `QDRANT_TIMEOUT` | Optional Qdrant pass-throughs, upstream names verbatim (defaults: off, `open-webui`, off, 6334, on, 5) |

`WEBUI_ADMIN_EMAIL` is **`env_require`** (mandatory, plaintext config), not an accepted
variable.

## Credential-backed Variables (secret_accept)

These resolve from the credential store and arrive as podman secrets
(`Secret=…,type=env,target=<VAR>`) — never plaintext in `charly.yml` or the quadlet. The
`key:` column is the store coordinate; several candies sharing one upstream credential all
resolve to the same stored value.

| Variable | Store key |
|----------|-----------|
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | `charly/api-key/openrouter` |
| `OLLAMA_API_KEY` | `charly/api-key/ollama` |
| `OPENAI_API_KEY` | `charly/api-key/openai` |
| `WHISPER_API_KEY` | `charly/api-key/whisper` |
| `QDRANT_API_KEY` | `charly/api-key/qdrant` (generated by the qdrant layer's `secret_require`) |

An optional `secret_accept` that does not resolve is **silently omitted**, which is why the
entrypoint treats `QDRANT_URL` without `QDRANT_API_KEY` as a startup error rather than a
degraded mode.

## Image generation (ComfyUI)

Open Web UI's image generation talks to a ComfyUI server through its `comfyui` engine. The candy sets
`IMAGE_GENERATION_ENGINE=comfyui` as a constant; the SERVER is per deploy, and generation stays OFF until an
operator turns it on, so a deploy with no ComfyUI behind it never advertises a broken feature.

**One caveat before the wiring.** `IMAGE_GENERATION_ENGINE` is an IMAGE-level default: an image built BEFORE
this contract carries no engine at all. On such an image, pass it explicitly (it is also an
`env_accept` row) or rebuild the image — otherwise the engine is unset and generation stays off even
though the URL is right. The same applies to any future change of the default.

Minimal wiring — a ComfyUI deployment and a URL (on an image built from this candy version):

```bash
# 1. the image server (its own deploy; a GPU is required)
charly deploy add comfyui comfyui
# 2. point Open Web UI at it
charly config openwebui -i lab -e WEBUI_ADMIN_EMAIL=you@example.com \
  -e COMFYUI_BASE_URL=http://charly-comfyui:8188 -e ENABLE_IMAGE_GENERATION=true
```

A ComfyUI deploy that declares `env_provide: COMFYUI_BASE_URL` injects the URL itself, in which case only
`ENABLE_IMAGE_GENERATION=true` is needed. On a pre-existing image add `-e IMAGE_GENERATION_ENGINE=comfyui`:
the default lives in the image, so an older image has none. Both pods must share a pod network for the DNS name to resolve —
that is what makes `http://<comfyui-deploy-name>:8188` work rather than a host port.

The generated images land in the deployment's own data volume through Open Web UI; ComfyUI's own
`/history` records the same prompt, which is how a round-trip is verified end to end.

## Secrets (Two-Tier Architecture)

### Tier 1: Infrastructure secrets (podman secrets via `secret:` field)

Auto-generated, stored in credential store (keyring/config-file fallback):

| Secret | Env Fallback | Purpose | Auto-gen path |
|--------|-------------|---------|---------------|
| `webui-secret-key` | `WEBUI_SECRET_KEY` | JWT + encryption key (CRITICAL: losing it breaks all sessions and OAuth tokens) | `charly config` time, `ProvisionPodmanSecrets` |
| `admin-password` | `WEBUI_ADMIN_PASSWORD` | Admin account password — declared as `secret_require:` | `charly deploy add` time, `ensureCandySecret` |

Provisioned as `Secret=charly-openwebui-<name>,type=env,target=<ENV>` in the quadlet. The entrypoint checks env vars first (from `type=env` injection), then file mounts at `/run/secrets/` as fallback.

**First-run admin login:** `WEBUI_ADMIN_PASSWORD` auto-generates as a 32-byte hex random value if not pre-set. To retrieve the auto-generated password and log in for the first time:

```bash
charly secrets get charly/secret WEBUI_ADMIN_PASSWORD
```

Override with a specific password before the first deploy:

```bash
charly secrets set charly/secret WEBUI_ADMIN_PASSWORD <password>
charly config openwebui  # picks up the override
```

### Tier 2: User API keys (GPG-encrypted `.secrets` file)

User-provided API keys stored via `charly secrets gpg`:

```bash
charly secrets gpg set OPENROUTER_API_KEY sk-or-xxx
charly config openwebui --env-file .secrets     # Decrypts + injects at config time
```

## Auto-Configuration Entrypoint

The `openwebui-entrypoint` runs on EVERY start (no sentinel — `ENABLE_PERSISTENT_CONFIG=false` means env vars always override database config):

1. **Reads secrets** from env vars (podman `type=env`) or `/run/secrets/` file mounts
2. **LLM provider detection** (each provider APPENDS to the plural, index-aligned
   `OPENAI_API_BASE_URLS` / `OPENAI_API_KEYS` lists, so OpenRouter, Ollama Cloud and a
   direct OpenAI-compatible endpoint can be live at once):
   - `OLLAMA_HOST` -> `ENABLE_OLLAMA_API=true` + `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` (native Ollama API)
   - `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` -> `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` + the key
   - `OLLAMA_API_KEY` -> `https://ollama.com/v1` + the key (Ollama Cloud)
   - `OPENAI_API_KEY` -> the key, against `OPENAI_API_BASE_URL` when set, else
     `https://api.openai.com/v1` (the key alone declares the provider)
3. **MCP server discovery** from `CHARLY_MCP_SERVERS` JSON -> builds `TOOL_SERVER_CONNECTIONS` JSON for Open WebUI
4. **Jupyter detection** — if a jupyter MCP server URL is found, sets `CODE_EXECUTION_ENGINE=jupyter`
5. **Execs** `open-webui serve`

### TOOL_SERVER_CONNECTIONS Format

The entrypoint translates charly's `CHARLY_MCP_SERVERS` format into Open WebUI's expected `TOOL_SERVER_CONNECTIONS` JSON:

```json
[{
  "type": "mcp",
  "url": "http://charly-jupyter:8888/mcp",
  "spec_type": "url", "spec": "", "path": "",
  "auth_type": "", "key": "",
  "config": {"enable": true},
  "info": {"id": "jupyter", "name": "jupyter", "description": "MCP: jupyter"}
}]
```

**Key fields**: `type` must be `"mcp"` (not `"openapi"`), `config.enable` must be `true`, and
`info.id` is the server's identity (Open Web UI keys the tool id, the connected-client map and
the access-control lookup on it) — an empty id collapses every MCP server onto one identity, so
the entrypoint sets it to the server name.

## Key Design Choice: `ENABLE_PERSISTENT_CONFIG=false`

This is the critical architectural decision. Without it, Open WebUI's database config overrides environment variables after the first admin-panel save. With it disabled, env vars ALWAYS win — so the entrypoint's dynamic configuration (LLM providers, MCP servers, Jupyter) works reliably on every restart. No sentinel-guarded config patching needed (unlike hermes).

## Important: No `port_relay` Needed

Open WebUI binds to `0.0.0.0:8080` by default. The `port_relay` field is only for services that bind to `127.0.0.1` (like Chrome DevTools on port 9222). Using `port_relay` with Open WebUI causes a socat/Open WebUI port conflict on eth0.

## Build Notes

- **pixi.toml** uses `[pypi-dependencies]` (NOT `[feature.default.pypi-dependencies]` — the `default` feature is reserved in pixi)
- Open WebUI is installed via `pip install open-webui` in the pixi environment (~500MB+ of dependencies)
- First startup takes ~30 seconds (Alembic DB migrations, model loading). supervisord `autorestart=true` handles transient failures.

## Usage

```yaml
# charly.yml
openwebui:
  base: fedora
  candy:
    - agent-forwarding
    - openwebui
    - '@github.com/opencharly/pod-dbus'
    - charly
  ports:
    - "8080:8080"
```
